title: Trench Cave-In Prevention
summary: One cubic yard of soil can weigh 3,000 pounds or more, so a cave-in can trap and kill in seconds. This talk covers competent-person inspection, protective systems, spoil setback, and never working alone.
talking_points: Never enter an unprotected or uninspected trench, even for a quick task. A trained competent person must inspect the trench and the area around it first.
Know and understand your employer's trench emergency plan.
Keep excavated soil and rock at least 2 feet back from the trench edge.
Never work alone in a trench, and never without a lookout standing by.
Make sure your employer provides trench protection. OSHA allows sloping or benching the walls, shoring, or shielding with supports or a trench box.
site_hazards_to_check: No protective system (sloping, benching, shoring, or shield) for a trench 5 feet deep or more
Spoil pile, tools, or equipment within 2 feet of the trench edge
No competent-person inspection since the last rain, vibration, or soil change
No safe way out within 25 feet of workers in a trench 4 feet deep or more
Workers in the trench with no lookout and no emergency plan
discussion_questions: Who is the competent person, and when did they last inspect this trench?
What protective system is in use, and is the spoil pile set back far enough?
Where is the ladder or ramp out, and who is the lookout today?
